en: In order to explain another mudrā, he says "atha" and so forth. Regarding "aṅgamudrā": it refers to the limb-mudrā. "Pulā" means the buttocks. "Guhyam" refers to the Yoginī. Having straightened the thumb and index finger and joined their tips together, while contracting the remaining fingers, this is the *dharmodaya*-mudrā. "Talam" refers to the sole of the foot; "of the hand" occurs in some cases. "Sūryam" (the sun) refers to the right limb, according to some. "Nadīm" (the river) [is indicated] by the gesture of drawing a curved line in the air with the hand.

Because it is demonstrated by means of a gesture (*mudrā*) consisting of the waving of two hands with fingers extended, as if mimicking a wave, it is called *samudrā*. The statement "one should show a single finger" is an elliptical expression referring to a man; the same applies later [in the text] as well. "Two fingers" means two fingers. This is the *pratimudrā*. The demonstration of the gesture of raising the left eyebrow is the *pratimudrā*.

The meaning is that the present purpose is the showing of a single unified gesture for the observation of the two—the master and the disciple—who are both skilled in the conduct of the pledge (*samaya*) and so forth, and who are the yogi and the yoginī.
